FINAL AWS CREDENTIAL REPAIR + FULL PRODUCTION VERIFICATION

Execute this on the EXISTING IVX Holdings project only.

Do not create a new app.
Do not create a new repository.
Do not create a second Render service.
Do not bypass AWS testing.
Do not report PASS until AWS authentication succeeds live.

CURRENT VERIFIED STATUS

PASS:
- GitHub
- Render
- Supabase
- AI provider
- Security/JWT
- Storage configuration

FAIL:
- AWS authentication
- Current live error:
  SignatureDoesNotMatch on sts:GetCallerIdentity

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE

Repair the AWS credential binding on the exact Render backend service serving:

https://api.ivxholding.com

Then redeploy and prove all 7/7 providers pass with real production evidence.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — IDENTIFY THE EXACT LIVE SERVICE
==================================================

1. Confirm the exact Render service connected to:
   api.ivxholding.com

2. Provide:
   - Render service name
   - Render service ID
   - environment
   - repository
   - branch
   - currently deployed commit SHA
   - latest deployment ID

3. Do not edit credentials in another service, preview environment, worker, or obsolete backend.

4. Prove the selected Render service is the one answering:
   GET https://api.ivxholding.com/health

==================================================
PHASE 2 — AUDIT AWS VARIABLE NAMES AND SOURCES
==================================================

Audit every possible AWS credential source used by the backend:

- AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
- AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
- AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
- AWS_REGION
- AWS_DEFAULT_REGION
- AWS_PROFILE
- AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE
- AWS_CONFIG_FILE

Also search the codebase and deployment configuration for:

- hardcoded AWS credentials
- obsolete AWS variable names
- duplicate environment variables
- Render environment groups
- service-level variables
- Dockerfile ENV values
- render.yaml values
- .env loading
- fallback credentials
- AWS profiles
- cached configuration
- old credentials injected into worker processes

Report exactly which source wins at runtime.

Do not expose any secret value.

For each variable, return only:

- variable name
- exists: yes/no
- source
- character length
- first 4 masked characters
- last 4 masked characters
- whitespace detected: yes/no
- newline detected: yes/no

==================================================
PHASE 3 — VERIFY THE ACCESS KEY PAIR
==================================================

1. Confirm AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY belong to the same active IAM access key.

2. Confirm the access key is:
   - active
   - not deleted
   - not disabled
   - not paired with an older secret
   - not copied with spaces or newline characters

3. Normalize the runtime values safely:
   - trim leading spaces
   - trim trailing spaces
   - remove accidental CR/LF characters
   - do not alter legitimate characters inside the secret

4. If AWS_SESSION_TOKEN exists but these are long-lived IAM credentials:
   - remove the stale session token
   - redeploy

5. If these are temporary AWS credentials:
   - verify the matching AWS_SESSION_TOKEN is present
   - verify it has not expired
   - replace the complete three-part credential set together

6. Do not rotate or replace credentials unnecessarily.

7. Only request a new credential pair if live verification proves that:
   - the access key is inactive,
   - the secret does not match,
   - the credential was revoked,
   - or the temporary session expired.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — CORRECT THE EXACT RENDER VARIABLES
==================================================

On the exact production Render service:

1. Delete the current value of:
   AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID

2. Re-enter the confirmed correct access key ID.

3. Delete the current value of:
   AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

4. Re-enter the confirmed matching secret access key.

5. Set the correct region consistently:

   AWS_REGION=<actual IVX AWS region>
   AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=<same actual IVX AWS region>

6. Remove conflicting or obsolete AWS variables.

7. Verify the variable names are exact and case-sensitive.

8. Save the environment changes.

9. Trigger a clean production redeploy.

10. Do not rely only on a restart if Render requires a new deployment to inject updated variables.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — ADD SAFE RUNTIME DIAGNOSTICS
==================================================

Add or verify a safe AWS diagnostic that reports:

- credential provider selected
- access key present: true/false
- secret present: true/false
- session token present: true/false
- region
- access key length
- secret key length
- access key masked suffix
- process boot time
- deployment commit
- traceId
- AWS error code
- AWS HTTP status

Never print:

- full access key
- full secret key
- session token
- authorization header
- signed request

==================================================
PHASE 6 — TEST AWS DIRECTLY IN THE LIVE CONTAINER
==================================================

After the new deployment is live, run a real AWS identity test from the production container using the same runtime environment as the application:

aws sts get-caller-identity

Or the equivalent AWS SDK call:

STS GetCallerIdentity

Expected result:

- HTTP 200
- Account returned
- ARN returned
- UserId returned
- no SignatureDoesNotMatch
- no InvalidClientTokenId
- no ExpiredToken
- no AccessDenied

Mask sensitive identity details in the final report when appropriate.

If the test still fails, classify the exact error:

A. SignatureDoesNotMatch
- mismatched access key/secret
- secret formatting problem
- wrong credential source

B. InvalidClientTokenId
- invalid or inactive access key
- stale session token

C. ExpiredToken
- temporary credentials expired

D. AccessDenied
- authentication succeeded but IAM permissions are insufficient

Do not describe all failures as a generic credential problem.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — VERIFY S3 AND CLOUDFRONT
==================================================

After STS passes, verify the actual IVX AWS operations:

1. S3:
   - identify configured bucket
   - confirm bucket exists
   - confirm application can access the required prefix
   - perform a safe read/list test
   - perform a temporary upload test when permitted
   - read back the test object
   - delete the test object

2. CloudFront:
   - identify configured distribution
   - confirm distribution exists
   - confirm status is Deployed
   - confirm configured domain responds
   - verify an IVX asset resolves successfully

3. Do not declare storage PASS merely because variable names exist.

4. Storage PASS requires a real AWS-authenticated operation.

==================================================
PHASE 8 — RE-RUN ALL PROVIDER TESTS
==================================================

Run all seven tests live again:

1. GitHub
2. Render
3. Supabase
4. AWS
5. AI provider
6. Security/JWT
7. Storage: S3 + CloudFront

Required result:

7/7 PASS

For each provider provide:

- timestamp
- endpoint or operation tested
- HTTP/result status
- traceId
- verdict
- concise evidence

==================================================
PHASE 9 — RE-RUN THE OWNER-AUTHORIZED WORKER FLOW
==================================================

After AWS is fixed, rerun the complete owner-authorized IVX Senior Developer job:

1. Create real job.
2. Worker accepts job.
3. Job enters processing.
4. Protected endpoints authenticate correctly.
5. Job reaches LIVE_VERIFYING.
6. AWS verification returns PASS.
7. Deployment verification completes.
8. Job reaches COMPLETED/PASS.

Do not bypass the QA-only route.
Do not substitute a narrative report for execution.

==================================================
PHASE 10 — FINAL PRODUCTION PROOF
==================================================

Return one final evidence report containing:

PRODUCTION IDENTITY
- GitHub repository
- branch
- GitHub HEAD SHA
- Render service name
- Render service ID
- Render deployment ID
- Render live commit SHA
- deployment timestamp
- boot timestamp
- application version

HEALTH
- /health URL
- HTTP 200
- live commit
- build version
- boot time

AWS
- STS result: PASS
- AWS account masked
- ARN masked
- active region
- credential source
- S3 test: PASS
- CloudFront test: PASS
- previous SignatureDoesNotMatch: RESOLVED

PROVIDER MATRIX
- GitHub: PASS
- Render: PASS
- Supabase: PASS
- AWS: PASS
- AI: PASS
- Security: PASS
- Storage: PASS

WORKER
- job ID
- task ID
- final state
- verification timestamp
- HTTP 200 evidence
- final PASS evidence

==================================================
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
==================================================

The task is complete only when all are true:

- Exact production Render service was updated.
- AWS credential pair is confirmed and correctly bound.
- No stale AWS_SESSION_TOKEN interferes.
- No duplicate credential source overrides Render variables.
- STS GetCallerIdentity returns HTTP 200.
- S3 performs a real authenticated operation.
- CloudFront is verified live.
- All seven providers show 7/7 PASS.
- Owner-authorized worker completes end-to-end.
- GitHub HEAD matches Render live commit.
- /health returns HTTP 200 with current commit.
- No SignatureDoesNotMatch remains.
- No fake, assumed, partial, or narrative-only PASS.

Do not ask me to repeat credentials already stored unless runtime verification proves they are invalid, inactive, expired, revoked, or mismatched.

Execute now and continue until the final result is verified 7/7 PASS.
